 Texas $1,500 Checks: Will lawmakers back Governor-elect Gina Hinojosa’s plan and who could qualify?
 Texas $1,500 Checks: Will lawmakers back Governor-elect Gina Hinojosa’s plan and who could qualify?
 Synopsis
 Texas Governor-elect Gina Hinojosa wants to send a one-time $1,500 check to every household in the state. Her plan would draw billions from the state’s emergency reserve and needs approval from Texas lawmakers.
 By Aastha Raj , Global Desk Nov 05, 2026, 10:03:00 PM IST Follow us Gina Hinojosa campaigned on a promise to send every Texas household a $1,500 check. Now that she has flipped the seat and defeated Republican Gov. Greg Abbott, her supporters are looking at her with hope that she is going to fulfill her promise. To deliver on her words, the first thing Hinojosa has to do is to persuade lawmakers to pay for it. The governor-elect wants to take $17 billion from the state’s Rainy Day Fund which is a huge amount for the government. She has argued that Texans could use the money now to cover bills like rent and groceries. The Legislature has yet to approve the spending or decide who would qualify. For now, there’s no date for checks to go out.
 ADVERTISEMENT What is Gina Hinojosa’s $1,500 refund plan?
Hinojosa told KPRC’s ENOUGH that she wants each Texas household to receive $1,500. Her campaign calls it a “corruption tax refund.” The proposal is for a single payment. It would not create a recurring benefit.
The money would come from the Texas Economic Stabilization Fund, better known as the Rainy Day Fund. Hinojosa put the reserve at about $27 billion in the interview. Using $17 billion for the checks would leave about $10 billion, based on her figures. Lawmakers would have to decide whether the relief is worth drawing down that much of the reserve.

 Can the Texas governor send checks without lawmakers?
No. The Texas Legislature would have to authorize the spending. Hinojosa has said she would declare an affordability emergency on her first day in office and ask lawmakers to act. The declaration would open the debate. It would not release the money.
Under the Texas Constitution⁠, spending from the reserve under its general-purpose provision requires approval from two-thirds of the members present in each chamber. Hinojosa has pitched the checks as an idea that could win support from both parties. Some lawmakers may welcome a payment they can point to back home. Others may want to preserve more of the fund for a future budget shortfall.
 ADVERTISEMENT Who would qualify for the $1,500 Texas checks?
There is no official announcement regarding the eligibility rules for now. It can be expected once the governor-elect takes charge. She had said during the campaign that “every household” is the promise and right now the real question is: Will she be able to deliver the $1,500 checks? A bill would have to clarify on the eligibility rules and who all are going to receive it. 
You can understand it with this example: If there are two people living in one apartment and they are adults, they might be keeping their finances separate. So are they both eligible for the $1500 check or will only the address be considered. The lawmakers will have to outline these confusions and bring clarity to people as the answer would affect the cost for the government. 
 ADVERTISEMENT ADVERTISEMENT 
At $1,500 each, $17 billion would cover about 11.3 million payments before administrative expenses. The state would also need a diligent process to verify the residence of the receivers so there is no duplication or double payments. Those decisions will determine whether checks can go out automatically or whether some Texans would need to apply.
 When could Texas send the $1,500 payments?
There is no payment date. Hinojosa is scheduled to take office in January 2027. The first thing to watch is whether lawmakers introduce a bill. Its text would show how much they’re willing to spend and who would get the money. Even if the proposal clears both chambers, state officials would still need time to set up distribution.
 ADVERTISEMENT 
 FAQs
 Have the $1,500 checks been approved? 
No. They remain a proposal from Texas Governor-elect Gina Hinojosa.
 ADVERTISEMENT Is there an application portal? 
No official portal has been announced. Texas has not decided whether people would need to apply.
